Timing
Recorded times: second alteplase infusion started 19:25; coagulation sample drawn 20:13; results reported 21:06. Derived times: each infusion lasted approximately one hour, so estimated completion is 20:25; the team reported UFH restarted approximately one hour after the 19:25 start, giving an estimated restart of 20:25. The 20:13-to-report delay is 53 minutes. The estimated restart preceded the 21:06 report, so the aPTT 58.9 s result could not have informed the restart decision. Uncertainty remains because no independent exact restart timestamp exists.

Evidence and risks
The 11:55 platelet count (21 × 10⁹/L) is recorded. Two apheresis platelet doses were transfused 14:50–15:10. No post-transfusion count immediately before the 17:00 first alteplase is supplied, so the platelet count at first alteplase initiation is unknown. The 17:39 count (62 × 10⁹/L) is recorded but cannot be attributed solely to transfusion effect; confounders include consumption, dilution, and ongoing thrombosis. Fibrinogen fell from 1.38 to 1.07 g/L between 17:39 and 20:13, and aPTT rose from 47.5 to 58.9 s, suggesting progressive coagulopathy during alteplase.

Missing record
Most useful missing items: result-reporting times for the 11:55 and 17:39 samples; a post-transfusion platelet count before first alteplase; exact second-infusion completion and UFH restart timestamps; patient-specific anticoagulation target; documented evidence used at restart; and subsequent clinical course with safety adjudication.

D1.reason: The submission is accurate throughout and grounded in the supplied record. It correctly labels recorded times (19:25 infusion start, 20:13 sample, 21:06 report) versus derived times (20:25 estimated restart, derived from the team's 'approximately one hour after 19:25' account), and correctly calculates the 20:13-to-21:06 report delay as 53 minutes. It appropriately preserves uncertainty about the actual restart timestamp and notes that, on the derived estimate, the aPTT 58.9 s result was reported after the estimated restart, so the record does not establish that it informed the restart decision. Its handling of platelet data is also correct: the 17:39 count of 62 × 10⁹/L cannot establish the post-transfusion count at the 17:00 first alteplase initiation, and the rise cannot be attributed specifically to transfusion given confounders. It avoids inventing exact completion/restart times, does not prescribe a regimen, and does not infer safety from unprovided outcomes. It explicitly acknowledges where evidence is uncertain (restart timing, availability of results, attribution of platelet rise), matching the Score 5 anchor.

D4c.reason: The submission presents events in correct sequence with explicit temporal anchors throughout: recorded times (19:25 infusion start, 20:13 sample, 21:06 report) are clearly distinguished from derived estimates (~20:25 completion/restart), the 53-minute reporting delay is calculated correctly, and the ordering of transfusion (14:50–15:10), first alteplase (17:00), 17:39 count, and second infusion is preserved without sequencing errors. This matches the Score 5 anchor: correct chronology with explicit temporal anchors.

D5u.reason: The submission distinguishes recorded times (19:25, 20:13, 21:06) from derived estimates (~20:25 completion/restart), names the source of uncertainty (no independent exact restart timestamp), correctly treats the 17:39 platelet count as unable to establish the count at 17:00 first alteplase or a transfusion-specific effect, and identifies concrete missing records that would reduce uncertainty. This meets the Score 4 anchor: confidence is largely calibrated to evidence strength and known/unknown are separated. It falls short of Score 5 because the conclusion that the aPTT 58.9 s result 'could not have informed the restart decision' overstates certainty — the restart time is only an estimate, so the report could plausibly have preceded an actual later restart; the reference explicitly requires preserving this uncertainty. This single overcalibrated claim, however, is not the wholesale false certainty of Score 1, so Score 4 is the best fit.
